- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes or bullish sentiment (especially when sentiment is 0.00 or low, but recent price action suggests momentum).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is 0.00 and recent price action shows consolidation or downward drift.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day spikes in sentiment (e.g., 0.40) — model should not overcorrect or overshoot in the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is 0.00 and price is trending upward, model should not assume continuation; instead, slightly reduce forecast to account for mean reversion.
- When sentiment is 0.00 and price is trending downward, model should not assume further decline; slightly increase forecast to avoid underestimating reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers — if model predicts >10% above recent 18-day average, flag for correction.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and model forecast is >10% above true outcome, reduce forecast by 10–20% for next period.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and model forecast is <10% below true outcome, increase forecast by 5–10% for next period.
- Do not assume sentiment will persist — if sentiment is 0.00 for 3+ days, model should adjust forecast to reflect lack of momentum.
- When sentiment is 0.00 and price is near recent 18-day mean, model should not forecast sharp moves — keep forecast within ±5% of mean.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next period.
- If model forecast is <10% below true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, increase forecast by 5–10% for next period.
